intent: Hold the open state of one tooltip and tie its trigger to the short visual hint that trigger shows on hover or keyboard focus.
typical_uses: A short label for an icon-only control
The full text behind a truncated label

dont_use_when.situation: Information a user needs to complete the task

instead.target: visible text on the page, next to the control
instead.note: A tooltip is supplementary: hovering opens it for mouse pointers only, and nothing links its text to the trigger for assistive technology, so touch and screen-reader users may never receive it.

dont_use_when.situation: A floating panel the user interacts with (links, buttons, form fields)
A preview of what a link points to, opened by hovering the link
A list of actions anchored to a trigger

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

The root wires no ARIA relationship between trigger and popup: the trigger receives no `aria-describedby` and the popup no `tooltip` role, so the popup's text is not announced as the trigger's name or description.
`disabled` on the root closes a tooltip that is open and keeps every trigger of this root from opening it, except a trigger that passes its own `disabled`, which takes precedence over the root's.

anti_patterns.dont: Leave an icon-only trigger without an accessible name, counting on the tooltip text to name it
anti_patterns.do_instead: Give the trigger an `aria-label` (or visible text) that matches the tooltip's content, so every user receives the same message

children.states: children is the root's content, either React nodes or a function of the active trigger's payload that returns them
children.because: `React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` - the function form receives `{ payload }` from whichever trigger opened the tooltip. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (such as a trigger hover, focus or press, an outside press or Escape). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<TooltipRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Tooltip.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this root
handle.because: `TooltipHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the tooltip's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled tooltip is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open tooltip is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

good.title: A labelled icon-only trigger with its hint
A kit Button as the trigger element

bad.title: An icon-only trigger named only by its tooltip
bad.why: The tooltip's text is not wired to the trigger for assistive technology, so a screen reader announces an unnamed button.
